answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with per-identity bonding: before it may vote or trade, each agent locks collateral in escrow, so identities are never free. To buy a thousand votes, an attacker cannot just spawn a thousand clones; each must post a separate bond, and cost climbs linearly with every fake account. Honest agents reclaim their bond plus a fee, while cheaters forfeit it all, so the ridge of trust holds. Even a patient foe spreading funds across the lagoon of many epochs still pays more than one forged vote is worth, turning that canyon of sunk cost into a wall.
